Split in Batches Turns the items into one item per batch: batch (from 1), batches, count and the items as a list. Split Out Turns a list in a field into one item per element.

docs.title: Network
docs.text: Node Description HTTP Request Sends one HTTP request per item. Respond to Webhook Answers the webhook call that started the execution (Webhook Trigger with 'Using respond node'). Send Email Sends one email per item over SMTP, optionally with the item's attachments.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Node Description Compression Packs attachments into a ZIP archive and unpacks ZIP archives into items or attachments; compresses and decompresses single attachments with GZip. Convert to File Turns items into a file attachment, e.g. Extract from File Turns an attached file (from a webhook, a mail, an HTTP response, Read File) into items: CSV, JSON, XML, text, and Excel with the Office plugin. Read File Reads files from a folder of the server: as an attachment, as text, or as items from JSON or CSV. Write File Writes files into a folder of the server: attachments or text (one file per item), or all items as JSON or CSV (one file).

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Node Description SQL Runs SQL against SQL Server, PostgreSQL or SQLite, once per input item.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: Node Description Run Script Runs one .bat/.cmd, PowerShell, Python or shell script from a folder released by the host, once per input item. Run Scripts Folder Runs the switched-on scripts of a folder released by the host, in order, once per input item. Run Scripts Repo Clones a repository of a configured Git server for the run and runs its switched-on scripts in order, with the repository root as working directory (PIPE_WORK_DIRECTORY).

docs.title: Utility
docs.text: Node Description Log Writes a message per item to the application log and passes the items on. No Operation Passes items through unchanged. Result Defines what a user sees in the portal at the end of the run: text, Markdown or a table.

docs.title: Credential types
docs.text: See Credential types.

docs.title: Credential types
docs.text: Credentials are stored encrypted. Nodes reference them by id; secret fields are never shown again after saving.

docs.title: SQL
docs.text:
Runs SQL against SQL Server, PostgreSQL or SQLite, once per input item. Query returns the rows as items, Execute the number of affected rows.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Connection (required)credentialId credential (Connection String) Connection String credential: which database (sqlserver, postgres or sqlite) and how to reach it. Databaseprovider one of: fromCredential, sqlServer, postgreSql, sqlite Kind of database; usually it comes from the credential. fromCredential: The database named in the credential (sqlserver, postgres or sqlite).sqlServer: Microsoft SQL Server or Azure SQL.postgreSql: PostgreSQL.sqlite: A SQLite file. In Advanced. Default: fromCredential. Operationoperation one of: query, execute Read rows, or change data. query: SELECT: every result row becomes an item.execute: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, …: one item with the number of affected rows. Default: query. SQL (required)sql code The statement; use @name for values, e.g. WHERE id = @id. They are passed as parameters, never inserted into the SQL text. Source code; {{ }} is not evaluated. Parametersparameters key/value pairs @name → value, e.g. id → {{ $json.id }}; evaluated per item. Timeout (seconds)commandTimeout integer Longest wait for a statement; 0 waits without limit. In Advanced. Default: 30. Example: Read the open orders of a customer

Runs once per input item; every row becomes an item. The value comes in as the parameter @customer, never as SQL text.

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "query",
  "sql": "SELECT id, amount FROM orders WHERE customer = @customer AND status = 'open'",
  "parameters": {
    "customer": "{{ $json.customer }}"
  }
}

Input:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 17,
    "amount": 120.5
  },
  {
    "id": 21,
    "amount": 80
  }
]
Example: Mark orders as shipped

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "execute",
  "sql": "UPDATE orders SET status = 'shipped' WHERE id = @id",
  "parameters": {
    "id": "{{ $json.id }}"
  }
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 17
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "affectedRows": 1
  }
]

docs.title: Compression
docs.text:
Packs attachments into a ZIP archive and unpacks ZIP archives into items or attachments; compresses and decompresses single attachments with GZip.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Operationoperation one of: zip, unzip, gzip, gunzip What to do with the attachments. zip: Pack attachments into a ZIP archive.unzip: Unpack a ZIP archive into its files.gzip: Compress one attachment into a .gz file.gunzip: Decompress a .gz attachment. Default: zip. Zipscope one of: eachItem, allItems One archive per item, or one of all items. eachItem: One archive per item with its attachments.allItems: One archive with the attachments of all items. Only when Operation is zip. Default: eachItem. Archive namefileName text File name of the archive, e.g. invoices.zip. Only when Operation is zip. Supports expressions. Unzip intooutput one of: itemPerEntry, attachments One item per file, or all files as attachments of the input item. itemPerEntry: One item per file in the archive, the file attached as data.attachments: The input item with every file of the archive as an attachment. Only when Operation is unzip. Default: itemPerEntry. AttachmentsbinaryProperty text Zip: names of the attachments to pack, separated by commas; empty packs all. Otherwise the one attachment to read, data if empty. In Advanced. Max size (MB)maxMegabytes integer Stop when the unpacked content gets larger; protects against archives that unpack to huge sizes. Only when Operation is unzip or gunzip. In Advanced. Default: 500. Result attachmentoutputProperty text Name of the attachment with the result, data if empty. Only when Operation is zip or gzip or gunzip. In Advanced. Example: Pack the files of all items into one ZIP

E.g. after Read File with invoices/*.pdf: one item comes out with the archive attached as data.

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "zip",
  "scope": "allItems",
  "fileName": "invoices.zip"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  },
  {
    "fileName": "2025-002.pdf",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "2025-002.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "count": 2,
    "entries": 2,
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "invoices.zip",
        "mimeType": "application/zip"
      }
    }
  }
]
Example: Unpack a ZIP archive

Every file of the archive becomes an item with the file attached as data, e.g. to read each one with Extract from File.

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "unzip"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "invoices.zip",
        "mimeType": "application/zip"
      }
    }
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
    "path": "2025-001.pdf",
    "size": 14,
    "modifiedAt": "2026-11-11T08:00:00.0000000+00:00",
    "archive": "invoices.zip",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  },
  {
    "fileName": "2025-002.pdf",
    "path": "2025-002.pdf",
    "size": 14,
    "modifiedAt": "2026-11-11T08:00:00.0000000+00:00",
    "archive": "invoices.zip",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "2025-002.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  }
]
Example: Compress a file with GZip

The attachment is replaced by its compressed version; the name gets .gz.

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "gzip"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "export.csv",
        "mimeType": "text/csv"
      }
    }
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "export.csv.gz",
        "mimeType": "application/gzip"
      }
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Convert to File
docs.text:
Turns items into a file attachment, e.g. to send it by mail, upload it or save it with Write File: CSV, JSON, XML, text, and Excel with the Office plugin.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Format (required)format text Format of the file. Excel needs the Office plugin. Filesmode one of: allItems, eachItem One file of all items, or one file per item. allItems: One file with all items; CSV and Excel always do this.eachItem: One file per item, attached to the item (JSON, XML, Text). Only when Format is json or xml or text. Default: allItems. File namefileName text Name of the file, e.g. orders.csv; empty: data plus the extension of the format. Supports expressions. Header rowheader true/false Write the column names as the first row. Only when Format is csv or xlsx. Default: true. Delimiterdelimiter text Character between the columns, e.g. , or ; or \t. Only when Format is csv. Sheetsheet text Name of the sheet, e.g. Orders. Only when Format is xlsx. Supports expressions. Sheet per fieldsheetPerField text One sheet per value of this field, e.g. region makes a sheet per region. Only when Format is xlsx. In Advanced. Root elementrootElement text Name of the outer element, e.g. orders; for one file per item, the element of the item. Only when Format is xml. Supports expressions. Item elementitemElement text Element of each item in one file of all items, e.g. order. Only when Format is xml. Text fieldtextField text Field of the items to write, one item per line, e.g. line. Only when Format is text. Encodingencoding text Character set of the file, e.g. utf-8, windows-1252, iso-8859-1, utf-16. Only when Format is csv or json or xml or text. In Advanced. Attachment namebinaryProperty text Name of the new attachment, under which later nodes find the file. In Advanced. Example: All items as one CSV file

One item comes out with the file attached as data, e.g. for Send Email or Write File.

Parameters:

{
  "format": "csv",
  "fileName": "orders.csv"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "customer": "Anna"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "customer": "Ben"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "format": "csv",
    "count": 2,
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "orders.csv",
        "mimeType": "text/csv"
      }
    }
  }
]
Example: One JSON file per item

Every item keeps its fields and gets its own file, named with an expression.

Parameters:

{
  "format": "json",
  "mode": "eachItem",
  "fileName": "order-{{ $json.id }}.json"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "customer": "Anna"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "customer": "Ben"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "customer": "Anna",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "order-1.json",
        "mimeType": "application/json"
      }
    }
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "customer": "Ben",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "order-2.json",
        "mimeType": "application/json"
      }
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Extract from File
docs.text:
Turns an attached file (from a webhook, a mail, an HTTP response, Read File) into items: CSV, JSON, XML, text, and Excel with the Office plugin. Runs once per input item.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Format (required)format text Format of the file. Excel needs the Office plugin. Outputoutput one of: items, field How the rows come out. items: One item per row or object; the fields of the input item are not kept.field: The input item stays one item and gets all rows or objects as a list in one field. Default: items. Fieldfield text Name of the field that gets the list, e.g. rows. Only when Output is field. Header rowheader true/false The first row holds the column names; otherwise the columns are column1, column2, …. Only when Format is csv or xlsx. Default: true. Delimiterdelimiter text Character between the columns, e.g. , or ; or \t; empty detects it from the first row. Only when Format is csv. Sheetsheet text Name of the sheet to read; empty reads the first. Only when Format is xlsx. Supports expressions. Item elementitemElement text Every element of this name becomes an item, e.g. order; empty makes the whole document one item. Only when Format is xml. Always arrayalwaysArray text Element names, separated by commas, that become lists even when they occur once, e.g. line. Only when Format is xml. In Advanced. Encodingencoding text Character set of the file, e.g. utf-8, windows-1252, iso-8859-1; a byte order mark wins. Only when Format is csv or json or xml or text. In Advanced. Attachment namebinaryProperty text Name of the attachment to read; data unless an earlier node named it differently. In Advanced. Example: Rows of an attached CSV file as items

E.g. after a Webhook Trigger with an upload or an Email Trigger: every row becomes an item. All values are text.

Parameters:

{
  "format": "csv",
  "delimiter": ";"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "orders.csv",
        "mimeType": "text/csv"
      }
    }
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": "1",
    "customer": "Anna"
  },
  {
    "id": "2",
    "customer": "Ben"
  }
]
Example: A JSON array into one field of the item

With Output 'All rows in one field' the item keeps its fields and gets the list, e.g. to count or loop over it later.

Parameters:

{
  "format": "json",
  "output": "field",
  "field": "lines"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "order": "A-17",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "lines.json",
        "mimeType": "application/json"
      }
    }
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "order": "A-17",
    "lines": [
      {
        "sku": "P-1",
        "qty": 2
      },
      {
        "sku": "P-7",
        "qty": 1
      }
    ],
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "lines.json",
        "mimeType": "application/json"
      }
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Read File
docs.text:
Reads files from a folder of the server: as an attachment, as text, or as items from JSON or CSV. Runs once per input item.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Folder (required)folder text Where the files are: one of the folders the administrator has set up for workflows. Path (required)path text File inside the folder, e.g. report.pdf; * and ? in the file name read all matching files, e.g. orders/*.csv. Supports expressions. Read asformat one of: binary, text, json, csv What becomes of the file content. binary: The file as an attachment, plus its name, size and date; for PDFs, images, ZIP archives.text: The content as text in the field text.json: Items from the JSON: an object becomes one item, an array one item per element.csv: One item per row; the first row holds the column names. Default: binary. CSV delimitercsvDelimiter text Character between the columns, e.g. , or ; or \t for tab. Only when Read as is csv. Include subfoldersincludeSubfolders true/false Only with * or ? in the path: search the subfolders too, e.g. orders/*.csv then also finds orders/2025/a.csv. In Advanced. Default: false. Attachment namebinaryProperty text Name under which later nodes find the file, e.g. in Write File or Send Email. Only when Read as is binary. In Advanced. Example: Read a CSV file as items

Every row becomes an item; the first row holds the column names. All values are text.

Given the file orders/2025-11.csv in the folder:

id;customer;amount
1;Anna;120.50
2;Ben;80.00

Parameters:

{
  "folder": "files",
  "path": "orders/2025-11.csv",
  "format": "csv",
  "csvDelimiter": ";"
}

Output:

[
  {
    "id": "1",
    "customer": "Anna",
    "amount": "120.50"
  },
  {
    "id": "2",
    "customer": "Ben",
    "amount": "80.00"
  }
]
Example: Read a PDF as an attachment

The file is attached to the item as data, e.g. to send it by mail or upload it; the item tells its name, size and date.

Given the file invoices/2025-001.pdf in the folder:

%PDF-1.7 (sample)

Parameters:

{
  "folder": "files",
  "path": "invoices/2025-001.pdf",
  "format": "binary"
}

Output:

[
  {
    "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
    "path": "invoices/2025-001.pdf",
    "size": 17,
    "modifiedAt": "2026-11-11T08:00:00.0000000Z",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  }
]
Example: Read all text files of a folder

With * in the path every matching file is read, one item per file, in the order of their names.

Given the file notes/a.txt in the folder:

Call Anna

Given the file notes/b.txt in the folder:

Order paper

Parameters:

{
  "folder": "files",
  "path": "notes/*.txt",
  "format": "text"
}

Output:

[
  {
    "fileName": "a.txt",
    "path": "notes/a.txt",
    "size": 9,
    "modifiedAt": "2026-11-11T08:00:00.0000000Z",
    "text": "Call Anna"
  },
  {
    "fileName": "b.txt",
    "path": "notes/b.txt",
    "size": 11,
    "modifiedAt": "2026-11-11T08:00:00.0000000Z",
    "text": "Order paper"
  }
]

docs.title: Write File
docs.text:
Writes files into a folder of the server: attachments or text (one file per item), or all items as JSON or CSV (one file).

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Folder (required)folder text Where to write: one of the folders the administrator has set up for workflows. Path (required)path text File inside the folder, e.g. export/orders.csv; missing subfolders are created. Supports expressions. Writecontent one of: binary, text, itemsAsJson, itemsAsCsv What goes into the file. binary: One file per item: the item's attachment, e.g. a PDF from Read File or a mail.text: One file per item with the text below.itemsAsJson: One file with all items as a JSON array.itemsAsCsv: One file with all items as CSV rows, one column per field. Default: binary. Texttext text Content of the file, e.g. Order {{ $json.id }} received. Only when Write is text. Supports expressions. CSV delimitercsvDelimiter text Character between the columns, e.g. , or ; or \t for tab. Only when Write is itemsAsCsv. If the file existsifExists one of: overwrite, append, fail What happens when the file is already there. overwrite: Replace the file.append: Add to the end of the file; CSV adds rows without a second header, JSON can't be appended.fail: Stop with an error and keep the file. Default: overwrite. Attachment namebinaryProperty text Name of the attachment to write; data unless an earlier node named it differently. Only when Write is binary. In Advanced. Example: Save all items as a CSV file

One file with a row per item. The output is one item that tells where the file is and how large it is.

Parameters:

{
  "folder": "files",
  "path": "export/orders.csv",
  "content": "itemsAsCsv"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "customer": "Anna"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "customer": "Ben"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "folder": "files",
    "path": "export/orders.csv",
    "size": 28
  }
]
Example: One text file per item

The path and the text use expressions, so every item gets its own file. The items go on with the field writtenFile.

Parameters:

{
  "folder": "files",
  "path": "messages/{{ $json.id }}.txt",
  "content": "text",
  "text": "Order {{ $json.id }} received"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 17
  },
  {
    "id": 18
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 17,
    "writtenFile": {
      "folder": "files",
      "path": "messages/17.txt",
      "size": 17
    }
  },
  {
    "id": 18,
    "writtenFile": {
      "folder": "files",
      "path": "messages/18.txt",
      "size": 17
    }
  }
]
Example: Archive an attachment

Saves the attachment of each item, e.g. a PDF from Read File or from a mail, under its own name.

Parameters:

{
  "folder": "files",
  "path": "archive/{{ $json.fileName }}",
  "content": "binary"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
    "writtenFile": {
      "folder": "files",
      "path": "archive/2025-001.pdf",
      "size": 17
    },
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "2025-001.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Execute Workflow
docs.text:
Runs another workflow with the items and outputs what its last node returned. Call it per item or per batch to loop.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Workflow (required)workflowId workflow The workflow to run; it starts with an Execute Workflow Trigger and doesn't have to be active. Call itmode one of: onceForAllItems, eachItem, batches How often the other workflow runs. onceForAllItems: One call with all items.eachItem: One call per item: the other workflow is the body of a loop.batches: One call per batch of items, e.g. 100 at a time. Default: onceForAllItems. Batch sizebatchSize integer Items per call, e.g. 100. Only when Call it is batches. Default: 10. Pause between calls (ms)delayMs integer Waits this long before each call but the first, e.g. 1000 for the rate limit of an API; 0 = no pause. Only when Call it is eachItem or batches. Default: 0. Example: A loop: one call per customer

The other workflow (here: 'Send reminder') gets one item per call; the output is what its last node returned, all calls together.

Parameters:

{
  "workflowId": "send-reminder",
  "mode": "eachItem",
  "delayMs": 1000
}

Input:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "open": 120
  },
  {
    "customer": "Ben",
    "open": 80
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "open": 120,
    "reminded": true
  },
  {
    "customer": "Ben",
    "open": 80,
    "reminded": true
  }
]

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Keeps only the items that match a condition.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Value 1value1 JSON The value to check, usually a field such as {{ $json.total }}. Supports expressions. Operationoperation one of: isEqual, notEqual, contains, notContains, greaterThan, greaterThanOrEqual, lessThan, lessThanOrEqual, isEmpty, isNotEmpty, isTrue, isFalse How Value 1 is checked. isEqual: Same value; numbers as numbers, text with case.notEqual: Different value.contains: Text contains the text, or a list contains the value.notContains: Text or list doesn't contain it.greaterThan: Numbers by value, text alphabetically.greaterThanOrEqual: Numbers by value, text alphabetically.lessThan: Numbers by value, text alphabetically.lessThanOrEqual: Numbers by value, text alphabetically.isEmpty: Missing, null, empty text or an empty list.isNotEmpty: Has a value.isTrue: true, a number other than 0 or a text like true or yes.isFalse: Everything that isn't true. Default: isEqual. Value 2value2 JSON The value to compare with, e.g. 100 or {{ $json.limit }}. Only when Operation is isEqual or notEqual or contains or notContains or greaterThan or greaterThanOrEqual or lessThan or lessThanOrEqual. Supports expressions. Example: Only orders above 100

Items that don't match are dropped.

Parameters:

{
  "value1": "{{ $json.amount }}",
  "operation": "greaterThan",
  "value2": 100
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "amount": 80
  },
  {
    "id": 3,
    "amount": 450
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "id": 3,
    "amount": 450
  }
]
Example: Only items with an email

Parameters:

{
  "value1": "{{ $json.email }}",
  "operation": "isNotEmpty"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "name": "Anna",
    "email": "anna@example.com"
  },
  {
    "name": "Ben",
    "email": ""
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "name": "Anna",
    "email": "anna@example.com"
  }
]

docs.title: If
docs.text:
Routes each item to 'true' or 'false' depending on a condition.

Inputs: main · Outputs: true, false

Parameter Type Description Value 1value1 JSON The value to check, usually a field such as {{ $json.total }}. Supports expressions. Operationoperation one of: isEqual, notEqual, contains, notContains, greaterThan, greaterThanOrEqual, lessThan, lessThanOrEqual, isEmpty, isNotEmpty, isTrue, isFalse How Value 1 is checked. isEqual: Same value; numbers as numbers, text with case.notEqual: Different value.contains: Text contains the text, or a list contains the value.notContains: Text or list doesn't contain it.greaterThan: Numbers by value, text alphabetically.greaterThanOrEqual: Numbers by value, text alphabetically.lessThan: Numbers by value, text alphabetically.lessThanOrEqual: Numbers by value, text alphabetically.isEmpty: Missing, null, empty text or an empty list.isNotEmpty: Has a value.isTrue: true, a number other than 0 or a text like true or yes.isFalse: Everything that isn't true. Default: isEqual. Value 2value2 JSON The value to compare with, e.g. 100 or {{ $json.limit }}. Only when Operation is isEqual or notEqual or contains or notContains or greaterThan or greaterThanOrEqual or lessThan or lessThanOrEqual. Supports expressions. Example: Large orders one way, the rest the other

Every item goes to exactly one output: true or false. Connect a node to each.

Parameters:

{
  "value1": "{{ $json.amount }}",
  "operation": "greaterThanOrEqual",
  "value2": 100
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "amount": 80
  }
]

Output true:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "amount": 120
  }
]

Output false:

[
  {
    "id": 2,
    "amount": 80
  }
]

docs.title: Merge
docs.text:
Waits for both inputs and merges their items.

Inputs: input1, input2 · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Modemode one of: append, combineByIndex How the items of the two inputs come together. append: The items of input 1, then the items of input 2.combineByIndex: Item 1 of both inputs becomes one item, item 2 the next, …; input 2 wins when both have a field. Default: append. Example: Append the items of both branches

E.g. after an If: both branches come together again.

Parameters:

{
  "mode": "append"
}

Input input1:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "route": "express"
  }
]

Input input2:

[
  {
    "id": 2,
    "route": "standard"
  },
  {
    "id": 3,
    "route": "standard"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "route": "express"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "route": "standard"
  },
  {
    "id": 3,
    "route": "standard"
  }
]
Example: Combine items by position

Item 1 of input 1 and item 1 of input 2 become one item, and so on.

Parameters:

{
  "mode": "combineByIndex"
}

Input input1:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "customer": "Anna"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "customer": "Ben"
  }
]

Input input2:

[
  {
    "status": "paid"
  },
  {
    "status": "open"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "customer": "Anna",
    "status": "paid"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "customer": "Ben",
    "status": "open"
  }
]

docs.title: Switch
docs.text:
Routes each item to the output of the first matching case.

Ports: depend on the parameters.

Parameter Type Description Valuevalue JSON The value that decides the output, usually a field such as {{ $json.country }}. Supports expressions. Casescases list of JSON One output per case, e.g. AT, DE, CH; items matching no case go to fallback. Example: One output per country

The outputs are case-0, case-1, … in the order of the cases; everything else goes to fallback.

Parameters:

{
  "value": "{{ $json.country }}",
  "cases": [
    "AT",
    "DE"
  ]
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "country": "DE"
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "country": "AT"
  },
  {
    "id": 3,
    "country": "CH"
  }
]

Output case-0:

[
  {
    "id": 2,
    "country": "AT"
  }
]

Output case-1:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "country": "DE"
  }
]

Output fallback:

[
  {
    "id": 3,
    "country": "CH"
  }
]

docs.title: Wait
docs.text:
Pauses the execution, then passes the items on. Waits in memory; a restart of the host ends the execution.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Wait foramount number How long, e.g. 30; the items go on unchanged afterwards. Default: 5. Unitunit one of: seconds, minutes, hours Unit of the time. seconds: Seconds.minutes: Minutes.hours: Hours; long waits are better done with a Cron Trigger. Default: seconds. Example: Wait a second before the next call

The items go on unchanged after the pause, e.g. to give another system time to finish.

Parameters:

{
  "amount": 1,
  "unit": "seconds"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 1
  }
]

docs.title: HTTP Request
docs.text:
Sends one HTTP request per item. Output: statusCode, headers, body.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Methodmethod text What the request does. URL (required)url text Address of the request, e.g. https://api.example.com/orders/{{ $json.id }}. Supports expressions. CredentialcredentialId credential (Basic Auth, Bearer Token, API Key Header, OAuth2 Client Credentials) Signs in at the server: user and password, a token, an API key header or OAuth2 client credentials. Query parametersquery key/value pairs Added to the URL as ?name=value, e.g. status → open; values are encoded. Bodybody JSON What to send: JSON such as { "name": "{{ $json.name }}" }, or text. Only when Method is post or put or patch or delete. Supports expressions. Content typecontentType text Kind of the body, e.g. application/json or text/plain. Only when Method is post or put or patch or delete. In Advanced. Supports expressions. Headersheaders key/value pairs Request headers, e.g. Accept → application/json. In Advanced. Response formatresponseFormat one of: auto, json, text How the answer is read into body. auto: JSON when the server says so, text otherwise.json: Read the answer as JSON.text: Keep the answer as text, e.g. HTML or CSV. In Advanced. Default: auto. Fail on HTTP error statusfailOnHttpError true/false Stop with an error when the server answers 400 or higher; off: the item goes on with the statusCode. In Advanced. Default: true. Pause between requests (ms)delayMs integer Waits this long before each request but the first, e.g. 1000 for the rate limit of an API; 0 = no pause. In Advanced. Default: 0. Example: Read an order from an API

One request per item; the answer replaces the item: statusCode, headers and body.

Parameters:

{
  "method": "GET",
  "url": "https://api.example.com/orders/{{ $json.id }}"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 17
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "statusCode": 200,
    "headers": {
      "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"
    },
    "body": {
      "id": 17,
      "customer": "Anna",
      "status": "paid"
    }
  }
]
Example: Send an item as JSON

POST with a body built from the item, e.g. to create a ticket in another system.

Parameters:

{
  "method": "POST",
  "url": "https://api.example.com/tickets",
  "body": {
    "title": "{{ $json.subject }}",
    "priority": "high"
  }
}

Input:

[
  {
    "subject": "Parcel never arrived"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "statusCode": 201,
    "headers": {
      "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
      "Location": "/tickets/981"
    },
    "body": {
      "id": 981,
      "title": "Parcel never arrived",
      "priority": "high"
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Respond to Webhook
docs.text:
Answers the webhook call that started the execution (Webhook Trigger with 'Using respond node'). The items pass through, so the workflow can continue after responding.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Respond withrespondWith one of: firstItem, allItems, customBody, noBody What the caller gets back. firstItem: The JSON of the first item.allItems: A list with the JSON of all items.customBody: The body below, e.g. { "ok": true }.noBody: Only the status code, no content. Default: firstItem. Bodybody JSON JSON or an expression, evaluated for the first item, e.g. {{ { ok: true, id: $json.id } }}. Only when Respond with is customBody. Supports expressions. Status codestatusCode integer HTTP status of the answer, e.g. 200 OK, 201 Created, 400 Bad Request. Default: 200. Headersheaders key/value pairs Response headers; a Content-Type other than JSON sends a text body as is, e.g. text/html. In Advanced. Example: Confirm an order to the caller

The webhook caller gets { "ok": true, "id": 17 } with status 201. The items pass on, so the workflow can go on after answering.

Parameters:

{
  "respondWith": "customBody",
  "body": "{{ { ok: true, id: $json.id } }}",
  "statusCode": 201
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 17,
    "customer": "Anna"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 17,
    "customer": "Anna"
  }
]

docs.title: Send Email
docs.text:
Sends one email per item over SMTP, optionally with the item's attachments.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description SMTP credential (required)credentialId credential (SMTP) The SMTP server and login used to send the mail. Fromfrom text Sender, e.g. Orders <orders@example.com>; empty: the sender of the credential. In Advanced. Supports expressions. To (required)to text Recipients, separated by commas, e.g. {{ $json.email }}. Supports expressions. Cccc text Copy to these addresses, separated by commas. In Advanced. Supports expressions. Bccbcc text Hidden copy to these addresses, separated by commas. In Advanced. Supports expressions. Subject (required)subject text e.g. Your order {{ $json.id }}. Supports expressions. Texttext text The message as plain text. Supports expressions. HTMLhtml text The message as HTML, sent next to the text or alone. In Advanced. Supports expressions. Attachmentsattachments list of text Names of the item's attachments to send, e.g. data; * sends all. Example: A confirmation per order, with the invoice attached

One mail per item. The item goes on with sentEmail, e.g. to log or store the message id.

Parameters:

{
  "to": "{{ $json.email }}",
  "subject": "Your order {{ $json.id }}",
  "text": "Hello {{ $json.customer }},\nthank you for your order. The invoice is attached.",
  "attachments": [
    "data"
  ]
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 17,
    "customer": "Anna",
    "email": "anna@example.com",
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "invoice-17.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 17,
    "customer": "Anna",
    "email": "anna@example.com",
    "sentEmail": {
      "messageId": "<a1b2c3@pipe>",
      "to": "anna@example.com",
      "subject": "Your order 17"
    },
    "$binary": {
      "data": {
        "fileName": "invoice-17.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Run Script
docs.text:
Runs one .bat/.cmd, PowerShell, Python or shell script from a folder released by the host, once per input item.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Script folderroot text One of the script folders the administrator has set up. Scriptscript text The file to run, from the chosen script folder. Argumentsarguments text Command line passed to every script, e.g. --date {{ $json.date }}. Supports expressions. Environment variablesenvironment key/value pairs Name → value; next to PIPE_ITEM, PIPE_WORKFLOW, PIPE_EXECUTION, PIPE_ENVIRONMENT and the variables of workflow, group and instance, which these override. In Advanced. CredentialcredentialId credential Its fields are passed as PIPE_CREDENTIAL_<FIELD>; their values are masked in output and logs. Error patternerrorPattern text A script also fails when a line of its output matches this regular expression, e.g. ^ERROR|Traceback. In Advanced. Ignore caseignoreCase true/false The error pattern ignores capitals, so ERROR also matches error. In Advanced. Default: true. Timeout per script (minutes)timeoutMinutes number A script that runs longer is stopped and fails. In Advanced. Default: 10. Example: Run a backup script

One run per input item; the output item tells whether it worked, with exit code and what the script printed.

Parameters:

{
  "root": "ops",
  "script": "backup.ps1",
  "arguments": "--target {{ $json.server }}"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "server": "db01"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "script": "backup.ps1",
    "success": true,
    "exitCode": 0,
    "reason": null,
    "matchedLine": null,
    "stdout": "Backup of db01 done: 2.1 GB\n",
    "stderr": "",
    "durationMs": 18420
  }
]

docs.title: Run Scripts Folder
docs.text:
Runs the switched-on scripts of a folder released by the host, in order, once per input item. One output item per script with exit code and output.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Script folderroot text One of the script folders the administrator has set up. Pathpath text File or folder inside the script folder; empty for all of it. Include subfoldersincludeSubfolders true/false Offer the scripts in the subfolders of the path too. Default: false. Scriptsscripts list Run top to bottom, each in its own process; files added later are off until switched on. Stop on first failurestopOnFirstFailure true/false Don't run the remaining scripts after one failed. Default: true. Argumentsarguments text Command line passed to every script, e.g. --date {{ $json.date }}. Supports expressions. Environment variablesenvironment key/value pairs Name → value; next to PIPE_ITEM, PIPE_WORKFLOW, PIPE_EXECUTION, PIPE_ENVIRONMENT and the variables of workflow, group and instance, which these override. In Advanced. CredentialcredentialId credential Its fields are passed as PIPE_CREDENTIAL_<FIELD>; their values are masked in output and logs. Error patternerrorPattern text A script also fails when a line of its output matches this regular expression, e.g. ^ERROR|Traceback. In Advanced. Ignore caseignoreCase true/false The error pattern ignores capitals, so ERROR also matches error. In Advanced. Default: true. Timeout per script (minutes)timeoutMinutes number A script that runs longer is stopped and fails. In Advanced. Default: 10. Example: The nightly scripts in order

One output item per script. When one fails, the node fails; with 'Stop on first failure' the rest doesn't run.

Parameters:

{
  "root": "ops",
  "path": "nightly/",
  "scripts": [
    {
      "value": "nightly/1-export.py",
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "value": "nightly/2-cleanup.sh",
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}

Output:

[
  {
    "script": "nightly/1-export.py",
    "success": true,
    "exitCode": 0,
    "reason": null,
    "matchedLine": null,
    "stdout": "Exported 1240 rows\n",
    "stderr": "",
    "durationMs": 5210
  },
  {
    "script": "nightly/2-cleanup.sh",
    "success": true,
    "exitCode": 0,
    "reason": null,
    "matchedLine": null,
    "stdout": "Removed 3 old files\n",
    "stderr": "",
    "durationMs": 140
  }
]

docs.title: Run Scripts Repo
docs.text:
Clones a repository of a configured Git server for the run and runs its switched-on scripts in order, with the repository root as working directory (PIPE_WORK_DIRECTORY). The clone is deleted afterwards.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Git serverserver text A Git server configured by the host. Repositoryrepository text A repository of the chosen Git server. Branchbranch text Empty for the repository's default branch. Pathpath text File or folder inside the repository; empty for all of it. Include subfoldersincludeSubfolders true/false Offer the scripts in the subfolders of the path too. Default: false. Scriptsscripts list Run top to bottom, each in its own process; files added later are off until switched on. Stop on first failurestopOnFirstFailure true/false Don't run the remaining scripts after one failed. Default: true. Argumentsarguments text Command line passed to every script, e.g. --date {{ $json.date }}. Supports expressions. Environment variablesenvironment key/value pairs Name → value; next to PIPE_ITEM, PIPE_WORKFLOW, PIPE_EXECUTION, PIPE_ENVIRONMENT and the variables of workflow, group and instance, which these override. In Advanced. CredentialcredentialId credential Its fields are passed as PIPE_CREDENTIAL_<FIELD>; their values are masked in output and logs. Error patternerrorPattern text A script also fails when a line of its output matches this regular expression, e.g. ^ERROR|Traceback. In Advanced. Ignore caseignoreCase true/false The error pattern ignores capitals, so ERROR also matches error. In Advanced. Default: true. Timeout per script (minutes)timeoutMinutes number A script that runs longer is stopped and fails. In Advanced. Default: 10. Example: Deployment scripts from Git

The repository is cloned for the run and deleted afterwards; each output item also names the commit that ran.

Parameters:

{
  "server": "gitea",
  "repository": "ops-scripts",
  "branch": "main",
  "scripts": [
    {
      "value": "deploy/update.ps1",
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}

Output:

[
  {
    "script": "deploy/update.ps1",
    "success": true,
    "exitCode": 0,
    "reason": null,
    "matchedLine": null,
    "stdout": "Updated 2 services\n",
    "stderr": "",
    "durationMs": 9310,
    "commit": "4f2c9a1"
  }
]

docs.title: Aggregate
docs.text:
Combines all items into a single item with lists. Attachments are not carried over.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Aggregatemode one of: allItemData, individualFields What to collect from the items. allItemData: One list with all items, e.g. to send them in one request.individualFields: One list per field with the values of all items, e.g. all email addresses. Default: allItemData. Put into fielddestination text Name of the field that gets the list, e.g. orders. Only when Aggregate is allItemData. Fieldsfields list of text Fields to collect, e.g. email or customer.name; items without the field are left out. Only when Aggregate is individualFields. Example: All items into one list

Three items become one item with a list, e.g. to send all orders in one HTTP request.

Parameters:

{
  "mode": "allItemData",
  "destination": "orders"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "amount": 80
  },
  {
    "id": 3,
    "amount": 45
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "orders": [
      {
        "id": 1,
        "amount": 120
      },
      {
        "id": 2,
        "amount": 80
      },
      {
        "id": 3,
        "amount": 45
      }
    ]
  }
]
Example: Collect the values of one field

One list per field, e.g. all addresses for one mail. Items without the field are left out.

Parameters:

{
  "mode": "individualFields",
  "fields": [
    "email"
  ]
}

Input:

[
  {
    "name": "Anna",
    "email": "anna@example.com"
  },
  {
    "name": "Ben"
  },
  {
    "name": "Cleo",
    "email": "cleo@example.com"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "email": [
      "anna@example.com",
      "cleo@example.com"
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
Transforms items with JavaScript, once for all items or once per item.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Modemode one of: allItems, eachItem How often the code runs. allItems: Runs once: items holds all input items, return an array of objects.eachItem: Runs per item with $json: return an object, or null to drop the item. Default: allItems. JavaScriptcode code Available: items (once for all), $json, $itemIndex (per item), $input, $node, $workflow, $execution, $now. Source code; {{ }} is not evaluated. Example: Sum up all items

Once for all items: items holds the JSON of every item; the returned array becomes the output items.

Parameters:

{
  "mode": "allItems",
  "code": "const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.amount, 0);\nreturn [{ count: items.length, total }];"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "amount": 80
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "count": 2,
    "total": 200
  }
]
Example: Change each item, drop some

Once per item: $json is the item; return null to drop it.

Parameters:

{
  "mode": "eachItem",
  "code": "if ($json.amount < 50) return null;\nreturn { ...$json, customer: $json.customer.toUpperCase() };"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "customer": "Ben",
    "amount": 30
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "customer": "ANNA",
    "amount": 120
  }
]

docs.title: Crypto
docs.text:
Hashes text or attachments (SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1, MD5), signs them with HMAC, creates UUIDs and encodes or decodes Base64. Writes the result into a field of each item.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Operationoperation one of: hash, hmac, uuid, base64Encode, base64Decode What to compute. hash: A checksum of text or a file, e.g. to detect changes.hmac: A signature with a secret key, e.g. to check or sign webhook calls.uuid: A new random id, e.g. 3f2b8c1e-….base64Encode: Text or a file as Base64 text.base64Decode: Base64 text back to plain text. Default: hash. Sourcesource one of: value, binary Work on the text in Value or on an attachment. value: The text in Value.binary: The content of an attachment, e.g. a file from Read File. Only when Operation is hash or hmac or base64Encode. Default: value. Valuevalue text Text to work on, e.g. {{ $json.body }}; ignored for an attachment. Only when Operation is hash or hmac or base64Encode or base64Decode. Supports expressions. Attachment namebinaryProperty text Name of the attachment, data unless an earlier node named it differently. Only when Source is binary. Algorithmalgorithm one of: sha256, sha512, sha1, md5 Hash function; SHA-256 unless a partner asks for another. sha256: The common choice.sha512: Longer and stronger.sha1: Only for checksums of old systems, not for security.md5: Only for checksums of old systems, not for security. Only when Operation is hash or hmac. Default: sha256. Secretsecret text The key, best from a secret variable, e.g. {{ $vars.WEBHOOK_SECRET }}. Only when Operation is hmac. Supports expressions. Outputoutput one of: hex, base64 How the result is written. hex: Lower-case hex digits, e.g. 2cf24d….base64: Base64 text, shorter. Only when Operation is hash or hmac. Default: hex. Target field (required)targetField text Field that gets the result, e.g. hash or signature. Example: SHA-256 checksum of a field

The item keeps its fields and gets the checksum, e.g. to notice when a text has changed.

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "hash",
  "value": "{{ $json.text }}",
  "targetField": "hash"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "text": "hello"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "text": "hello",
    "hash": "2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824"
  }
]
Example: Encode text as Base64

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "base64Encode",
  "value": "{{ $json.user }}:{{ $json.password }}",
  "targetField": "basic"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "user": "pipe",
    "password": "secret"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "user": "pipe",
    "password": "secret",
    "basic": "cGlwZTpzZWNyZXQ="
  }
]
Example: A new id per item

Every item gets its own random UUID.

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "uuid",
  "targetField": "id"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "id": "3f2b8c1e-5d47-4f0a-9b8e-2c6a1d7e4f90"
  }
]

docs.title: Date & Time
docs.text:
Gets the current time, formats, parses and calculates dates, and converts between time zones. Writes the result into a field of each item.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Operationoperation one of: now, format, parse, add, subtract, difference, convertTimeZone, startOf What to do with the date. now: The current date and time.format: A date as text in a pattern, e.g. 02.11.2026.parse: Text in a pattern to a date (ISO 8601).add: A date plus an amount of time, e.g. 14 days.subtract: A date minus an amount of time.difference: The time between two dates, in a unit.convertTimeZone: The same moment in another time zone.startOf: The start of the day, week, month … of a date. Default: format. Datevalue text The date: ISO 8601 like 2026-11-02T08:30:00+01:00, Unix seconds or milliseconds, or for Parse text in the pattern. Only when Operation is format or parse or add or subtract or difference or convertTimeZone or startOf. Supports expressions. Untiluntil text The second date; empty means now. The result is positive when it is later than Date. Only when Operation is difference. Supports expressions. Patternpattern text e.g. dd.MM.yyyy or yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm; empty: ISO 8601 (Format) or any common form (Parse). Only when Operation is format or parse. Supports expressions. Cultureculture text Language of month and day names, e.g. de-DE or en-US. Only when Operation is format or parse. In Advanced. Supports expressions. Amountamount number How many units, e.g. 14. Only when Operation is add or subtract. Default: 1. Unitunit one of: milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years Unit of the amount, the difference or the start. milliseconds: 1/1000 second.seconds: Seconds.minutes: Minutes.hours: Hours.days: Calendar days.weeks: 7 days; a week starts on Monday.months: Calendar months, whole numbers only.years: Calendar years, whole numbers only. Only when Operation is add or subtract or difference or startOf. Default: days. Time zonetimeZone text e.g. Europe/Vienna; Convert time zone: the target, Parse: the zone of text without offset, otherwise the zone to work in. Only when Operation is now or format or parse or convertTimeZone or startOf. Supports expressions. Target field (required)targetField text Field for the result, e.g. date or meta.due. Example: Due date 14 days after the invoice date

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "add",
  "value": "{{ $json.invoiceDate }}",
  "amount": 14,
  "unit": "days",
  "targetField": "dueDate"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "invoice": "R-17",
    "invoiceDate": "2026-11-02T08:30:00+01:00"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "invoice": "R-17",
    "invoiceDate": "2026-11-02T08:30:00+01:00",
    "dueDate": "2026-11-16T08:30:00+01:00"
  }
]
Example: Format a date for people

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "format",
  "value": "{{ $json.invoiceDate }}",
  "pattern": "dd.MM.yyyy",
  "targetField": "printed"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "invoiceDate": "2026-11-02T08:30:00+01:00"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "invoiceDate": "2026-11-02T08:30:00+01:00",
    "printed": "02.11.2026"
  }
]
Example: Days between two dates

Parameters:

{
  "operation": "difference",
  "value": "{{ $json.openedAt }}",
  "until": "{{ $json.closedAt }}",
  "unit": "days",
  "targetField": "days"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "ticket": 4711,
    "openedAt": "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z",
    "closedAt": "2026-11-05T12:00:00Z"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "ticket": 4711,
    "openedAt": "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z",
    "closedAt": "2026-11-05T12:00:00Z",
    "days": 3.5
  }
]

docs.title: Limit
docs.text:
Keeps only the first or the last N items.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Max itemsmaxItems integer How many items go on, e.g. 10; the rest is dropped. Default: 1. Keepkeep one of: firstItems, lastItems Which items are kept. firstItems: The items at the start, e.g. the newest after sorting by date descending.lastItems: The items at the end. Default: firstItems. Example: Keep the first two items

E.g. after Sort: only the top two go on.

Parameters:

{
  "maxItems": 2,
  "keep": "firstItems"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "product": "Lamp",
    "sold": 42
  },
  {
    "product": "Desk",
    "sold": 17
  },
  {
    "product": "Chair",
    "sold": 9
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "product": "Lamp",
    "sold": 42
  },
  {
    "product": "Desk",
    "sold": 17
  }
]

docs.title: Remove Duplicates
docs.text:
Keeps the first of several equal items (all fields equal, or the selected fields).

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Comparecompare one of: allFields, selectedFields When two items count as the same. allFields: Items are duplicates when all their fields are equal.selectedFields: Items are duplicates when the fields below are equal, e.g. the same email. Default: allFields. Fieldsfields list of text Fields that together identify an item, e.g. email or customer.id. Only when Compare is selectedFields. Example: One item per email address

The first item of each address is kept, later ones are dropped.

Parameters:

{
  "compare": "selectedFields",
  "fields": [
    "email"
  ]
}

Input:

[
  {
    "email": "anna@example.com",
    "source": "web"
  },
  {
    "email": "ben@example.com",
    "source": "web"
  },
  {
    "email": "anna@example.com",
    "source": "fair"
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "email": "anna@example.com",
    "source": "web"
  },
  {
    "email": "ben@example.com",
    "source": "web"
  }
]

docs.title: Set
docs.text:
Sets, renames or keeps fields of each item.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Fieldsfields key/value pairs Field (e.g. address.city) → value, e.g. Vienna or {{ $json.price * 1.2 }}. Renamerename key/value pairs Old field → new name, e.g. mail → email; done before the fields are set. Keep only set fieldskeepOnlySet true/false Drop all other fields: the items have only the fields set above. Default: false. Example: Add a calculated field and rename one

Values may be fixed or expressions; numbers stay numbers. Rename happens before the fields are set.

Parameters:

{
  "fields": {
    "gross": "{{ $json.net * 1.2 }}",
    "currency": "EUR"
  },
  "rename": {
    "mail": "email"
  }
}

Input:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "mail": "anna@example.com",
    "net": 100
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "net": 100,
    "email": "anna@example.com",
    "gross": 120,
    "currency": "EUR"
  }
]
Example: Keep only some fields

With 'Keep only set fields' everything else is dropped, e.g. before writing a CSV file.

Parameters:

{
  "fields": {
    "name": "{{ $json.customer.name }}",
    "city": "{{ $json.customer.address.city }}"
  },
  "keepOnlySet": true
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 7,
    "customer": {
      "name": "Anna",
      "address": {
        "city": "Graz",
        "zip": "8010"
      }
    }
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "name": "Anna",
    "city": "Graz"
  }
]

docs.title: Sort
docs.text:
Sorts the items by one or more fields: numbers by value, text alphabetically, missing values last.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Sort byfields list of text Fields in order of priority, e.g. customer, then date desc; desc sorts from high to low. Example: Highest amount first

Numbers are compared as numbers, so 120 comes before 80.

Parameters:

{
  "fields": [
    "amount desc"
  ]
}

Input:

[
  {
    "customer": "Ben",
    "amount": 80
  },
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "customer": "Cleo",
    "amount": 45
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "customer": "Ben",
    "amount": 80
  },
  {
    "customer": "Cleo",
    "amount": 45
  }
]

docs.title: Split in Batches
docs.text:
Turns the items into one item per batch: batch (from 1), batches, count and the items as a list. Attachments are not carried over.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Batch sizebatchSize integer Items per batch, e.g. 100; the last batch may have fewer. Default: 10. Put into fielddestination text Name of the field that holds the items of a batch, e.g. items. Example: Batches of two

Five items become three batches, e.g. to call Execute Workflow or an API with at most two items at a time.

Parameters:

{
  "batchSize": 2
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1
  },
  {
    "id": 2
  },
  {
    "id": 3
  },
  {
    "id": 4
  },
  {
    "id": 5
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "batch": 1,
    "batches": 3,
    "count": 2,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": 1
      },
      {
        "id": 2
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "batch": 2,
    "batches": 3,
    "count": 2,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": 3
      },
      {
        "id": 4
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "batch": 3,
    "batches": 3,
    "count": 1,
    "items": [
      {
        "id": 5
      }
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: Split Out
docs.text:
Turns a list in a field into one item per element.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Field to split out (required)field text A field with a list, e.g. orders or customer.addresses; every element becomes an item. Keep the other fields of the itemincludeOtherFields true/false Copy the other fields into every new item, e.g. the customer to each of their orders. Default: false. Example: One item per order line

The list lines becomes two items; with 'Keep the other fields' each line also gets the order number.

Parameters:

{
  "field": "lines",
  "includeOtherFields": true
}

Input:

[
  {
    "order": "A-17",
    "lines": [
      {
        "sku": "P-1",
        "qty": 2
      },
      {
        "sku": "P-7",
        "qty": 1
      }
    ]
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "order": "A-17",
    "sku": "P-1",
    "qty": 2
  },
  {
    "order": "A-17",
    "sku": "P-7",
    "qty": 1
  }
]
Example: A list of plain values

Values that aren't objects keep the name of the field.

Parameters:

{
  "field": "tags"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "tags": [
      "urgent",
      "billing"
    ]
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "tags": "urgent"
  },
  {
    "tags": "billing"
  }
]

docs.title: Cron Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow on a schedule while the workflow is active.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Cron expression (required)expression text When to run: minute hour day month weekday, e.g. 0 7 * * 1-5 is 7:00 on workdays, */15 * * * * every 15 minutes. Time zonetimeZone text Time zone of the schedule, e.g. Europe/Vienna. Example: Every workday at 7:00

While the workflow is active it starts at the given times with one item.

Parameters:

{
  "expression": "0 7 * * 1-5",
  "timeZone": "Europe/Vienna"
}

Output:

[
  {
    "timestamp": "2026-11-11T06:00:00.0000000+00:00",
    "expression": "0 7 * * 1-5"
  }
]

docs.title: Email Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow when unread mails are in a mailbox (IMAP), while the workflow is active. Checks at an interval; one run per check with one item per mail: sender, recipients, subject, date, text, html and the attachments as binary data. After the run has started the mails are marked as read, moved or deleted. Mails that are unread when the workflow is activated count.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Mail server (required)credentialId credential (IMAP Server) The mailbox to watch: an IMAP Server credential. Folderfolder text Mail folder to watch, e.g. INBOX or INBOX/Orders. From containsfromContains text Only mails from a sender with this text, e.g. @shop.example; empty: all. Subject containssubjectContains text Only mails with this text in the subject, e.g. Invoice; empty: all. After processingafterProcessing one of: markAsRead, moveToFolder, delete What happens to a mail once the run has started. markAsRead: The mail stays in the folder, marked as read.moveToFolder: The mail moves into the target folder, e.g. Done.delete: The mail is deleted. Default: markAsRead. Target foldertargetFolder text Folder for processed mails, e.g. Done; created if it doesn't exist. Only when After processing is moveToFolder. Download attachmentsdownloadAttachments true/false Attach the files of the mail to the item as attachment1, attachment2, …. Default: true. Max message size (MB)maxMessageSizeMb integer A larger mail is reported with its header only (tooLarge) and handled like the others. In Advanced. Default: 25. Check every (seconds)intervalSeconds integer How often the mailbox is checked. In Advanced. Default: 60. Example: Invoices arriving by mail

One item per unread mail; the PDF is attached as attachment1, e.g. for Write File or the AI node.

Parameters:

{
  "folder": "INBOX",
  "subjectContains": "Invoice",
  "afterProcessing": "moveToFolder",
  "targetFolder": "Done"
}

Output:

[
  {
    "messageId": "<4711@shop.example>",
    "uid": 4711,
    "folder": "INBOX",
    "from": {
      "name": "Shop",
      "address": "billing@shop.example"
    },
    "to": [
      {
        "name": null,
        "address": "pipe@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "cc": [],
    "subject": "Invoice R-17",
    "date": "2026-11-11T08:00:00.0000000+01:00",
    "text": "Please find the invoice attached.",
    "html": null,
    "attachments": [
      "R-17.pdf"
    ],
    "tooLarge": false,
    "$binary": {
      "attachment1": {
        "fileName": "R-17.pdf",
        "mimeType": "application/pdf"
      }
    }
  }
]

docs.title: Error Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow when a triggered run of a workflow that uses it as error workflow fails (set on the workflow, its group or the instance). Outputs { workflow, execution, node, subWorkflow, suppressed } of the failed run; execution.url links to it when Pipe:PublicUrl is set.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Throttle minutesthrottleMinutes integer Per failed workflow, start at most once in this time; failures in between are counted in 'suppressed' of the next run. 0 reports every failure. Default: 15. Example: A run of another workflow failed

Use it in an error workflow, e.g. to send a mail to the team. node tells which node failed; suppressed counts the failures held back by the throttle.

Parameters:

{
  "throttleMinutes": 60
}

Output:

[
  {
    "workflow": {
      "id": "import-orders",
      "name": "Import orders"
    },
    "execution": {
      "id": "6f1d0c",
      "mode": "trigger",
      "environment": "PROD",
      "startedAt": "2026-11-11T07:00:00.0000000+00:00",
      "error": "HTTP 503 from https://api.example.com/orders"
    },
    "node": {
      "id": "http",
      "name": "Load orders",
      "error": "HTTP 503 from https://api.example.com/orders"
    },
    "suppressed": 0
  }
]

docs.title: Execute Workflow Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow when another workflow calls it with Execute Workflow; outputs the caller's items.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

This node has no parameters.

Example: The items of the caller

Another workflow calls this one with Execute Workflow; its items arrive here unchanged. The output of the last node goes back to the caller.

Output:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "open": 120
  }
]

docs.title: File Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow when new files appear in a folder released by the host, while the workflow is active. Checks the folder at an interval and reports a file once it is complete. One run per check, with one item per file: folder, path, name, size, modified and event. Files that exist when the workflow is activated are not reported. Read File reads the content.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Folder (required)folder text Which folder to watch: one of the folders the administrator has set up for workflows. Pathpath text A subfolder of the folder, e.g. incoming; empty for the folder itself. File patternpattern text Which files count, e.g. .csv or order-.xml; * for all. Include subfoldersincludeSubfolders true/false Watch the subfolders of the path too. In Advanced. Default: false. Eventsevents one of: created, createdOrChanged Which files start the workflow. created: Only files that weren't there before.createdOrChanged: New files, and files whose size or time changed. Default: created. Check every (seconds)intervalSeconds integer A file is reported when it was unchanged in two checks in a row, so it comes after up to two intervals. In Advanced. Default: 10. Example: New CSV files in the incoming folder

One run per check with one item per new file. The file isn't read yet: Read File with {{ $json.path }} reads it.

Parameters:

{
  "folder": "files",
  "path": "incoming",
  "pattern": "*.csv",
  "events": "created"
}

Output:

[
  {
    "folder": "files",
    "path": "incoming/orders-17.csv",
    "name": "orders-17.csv",
    "size": 2048,
    "modified": "2026-11-11T08:00:00.0000000+00:00",
    "event": "created"
  }
]

docs.title: Form Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow from the user portal: declares the form the user fills in and outputs one item with the values. Without a Form Trigger a published workflow starts without input.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Fieldsfields list of JSON The inputs of the form. Each has a name (the property in the item), a label, a type (text, multiline text, number, boolean, date, choice or password), and optionally a description, a placeholder, a default, a regular expression the text must match as a whole (with the message shown otherwise) and the values of a choice. Example: A request form in the portal

The portal shows the fields; when the user sends the form, the workflow starts with one item of the values, named as the fields.

Parameters:

{
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "customer",
      "label": "Customer",
      "type": "text"
    },
    {
      "name": "amount",
      "label": "Amount",
      "type": "number"
    },
    {
      "name": "urgent",
      "label": "Urgent",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  ]
}

Output:

[
  {
    "customer": "Anna",
    "amount": 120,
    "urgent": true
  }
]

docs.title: Manual Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow when it is run from the editor.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

This node has no parameters.

Example: Start from the editor

Run or Test in the editor starts here with one empty item; the next nodes add the data.

Output:

[
  {}
]

docs.title: Recovery Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow when a workflow that failed and was reported to this error workflow runs successfully again (triggered runs only). Outputs { workflow, execution, failedSince, failedExecution, failures }; execution.url and failedExecution.url link to the runs when Pipe:PublicUrl is set.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

This node has no parameters.

Example: A failing workflow works again

Use it next to an Error Trigger, e.g. to send an all-clear mail.

Output:

[
  {
    "workflow": {
      "id": "import-orders",
      "name": "Import orders"
    },
    "execution": {
      "id": "8a2e41"
    },
    "failedSince": "2026-11-11T07:00:00.0000000+00:00",
    "failedExecution": {
      "id": "6f1d0c"
    },
    "failures": 3
  }
]

docs.title: Webhook Trigger
docs.text:
Starts the workflow when its URL is called while the workflow is active.

Inputs: none (starts the workflow) · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Path (required)path text Last part of the URL: the workflow is called at /webhook/<path>, e.g. orders/new; unique across active workflows. HTTP methodmethod one of: any, get, post, put, patch, delete Which calls start the workflow. any: Every method.get: Calls without a body, e.g. from a link.post: Calls with a body, e.g. forms and other systems; the usual choice.put: PUT calls.patch: PATCH calls.delete: DELETE calls. Default: post. RespondresponseMode one of: immediately, whenFinished, usingRespondNode When and with what the caller gets an answer. immediately: Answer 202 with the execution id at once; the workflow runs in the background.whenFinished: Wait for the run and answer with the items of the last node.usingRespondNode: Wait until a Respond to Webhook node answers. Default: immediately. Wait timeout (seconds)timeoutSeconds integer After this time the caller gets 202 and the run goes on; time in the queue counts, and a run still queued then gets 503 and leaves the queue. Only when Respond is whenFinished or usingRespondNode. In Advanced. Default: 30. CredentialcredentialId credential (Basic Auth, Bearer Token, API Key Header) Callers must authenticate with it; without one the webhook is public. Example: Receive an order from a shop

The shop sends POST /webhook/orders/new with JSON; the item holds method, path, query, headers, body and the time. Uploaded files arrive as attachments.

Parameters:

{
  "path": "orders/new",
  "method": "post",
  "responseMode": "immediately"
}

Output:

[
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "path": "orders/new",
    "query": {},
    "headers": {
      "Content-Type": "application/json"
    },
    "body": {
      "id": 17,
      "customer": "Anna",
      "amount": 120
    },
    "receivedAt": "2026-11-11T08:00:00.0000000+00:00"
  }
]

docs.title: Log
docs.text:
Writes a message per item to the application log and passes the items on.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Messagemessage JSON What to write per item, e.g. Order {{ $json.id }} received; {{ $json }} writes the whole item. Supports expressions. Levellevel one of: trace, debug, information, warning, error, critical, none How important the message is; the host decides which levels are kept. trace: Very detailed, usually switched off.debug: Details for finding errors.information: Normal messages.warning: Something unexpected that didn't stop the run.error: Something failed.critical: Something failed badly.none: Write nothing; the items just pass. Default: information. Example: Write a line per order

The log gets 'Order 17 received'; the items pass unchanged.

Parameters:

{
  "message": "Order {{ $json.id }} received",
  "level": "information"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 17
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 17
  }
]

docs.title: No Operation
docs.text:
Passes items through unchanged.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

This node has no parameters.

Example: Pass the items on

Useful as a placeholder or as a point where several branches meet.

Input:

[
  {
    "id": 1
  },
  {
    "id": 2
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "id": 1
  },
  {
    "id": 2
  }
]

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Defines what a user sees in the portal at the end of the run: text, Markdown or a table. Without a Result node the portal shows only the status. Outputs one item with the result, so place it at the end of the workflow.

Inputs: main · Outputs: main

Parameter Type Description Kindkind one of: text, markdown, table What the portal user sees. text: A plain message, e.g. Done: 17 rows.markdown: Formatted text with headings, lists and links.table: The incoming items, one row per item. Default: text. Titletitle text Heading above the result, e.g. Import finished. Supports expressions. Contentcontent text The message, e.g. Done: {{ $json.count }} rows; evaluated for the first incoming item. Only when Kind is text or markdown. Supports expressions. Error messageerrorMessage text Shown to the portal user when the run fails. Without it the user sees a general message and the number of the run; details of errors stay with the admins. Supports expressions. Example: A message for the portal user

The output item describes what the portal shows; put the node at the end of the workflow.

Parameters:

{
  "kind": "text",
  "title": "Import finished",
  "content": "{{ $json.count }} orders imported"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "count": 17
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "kind": "text",
    "title": "Import finished",
    "text": "17 orders imported"
  }
]
Example: The items as a table

Parameters:

{
  "kind": "table",
  "title": "Open invoices"
}

Input:

[
  {
    "invoice": "R-17",
    "amount": 120
  },
  {
    "invoice": "R-18",
    "amount": 80
  }
]

Output:

[
  {
    "kind": "table",
    "title": "Open invoices",
    "columns": [
      "invoice",
      "amount"
    ],
    "rows": [
      [
        "R-17",
        "120"
      ],
      [
        "R-18",
        "80"
      ]
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: gView.Pipe
docs.text: gView.Pipe ist eine Workflow-Anwendung: Im Editor verbindest du Nodes, und Items fließen von Node zu Node. Ein Workflow startet nach Zeitplan, über einen Webhook oder von Hand.

docs.title: Wo anfangen
docs.text:
• Anwenderhandbuch: Workflows bauen, ausführen und überwachen.
  • Administratorhandbuch: gView.Pipe installieren, konfigurieren und betreiben.
  • Entwicklerhandbuch: eigene Nodes als Plugins schreiben (nur auf Englisch).

docs.title: Versionshinweise
docs.text:
Was in jeder Version neu ist und was du beim Update tun musst. Die vollständige Liste der Änderungen steht im Changelog im Repository (englisch).

Ein Update ersetzt den Versionsordner des ZIP oder das Docker-Image. Die Ordner data, files und scripts sowie der Ordner _config bleiben, wie sie sind. Sichere sie vor dem Update (siehe Betrieb).
Die erste Version.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Ein visueller Editor für Workflows aus Nodes, die JSON-Items weiterreichen; der Editor zeigt Eingabe, Ausgabe und Log jedes Nodes.
  • Die Formulare der Nodes erklären jedes Feld und jede Wahl und zeigen nur, was zutrifft; jeder Node hat Beispiele seiner Ein- und Ausgabe im Editor und in der Node-Referenz.
  • Trigger: manuell, Cron, Webhook und Formular; Webhooks können wie eine kleine API antworten. Siehe Trigger und Webhooks.
  • JavaScript-Ausdrücke in jedem Parameter und ein Code-Node, ausgeführt in einer Sandbox.
  • Variablen und Environments, Gruppen, Sub-Workflows, Error-Workflows und Benachrichtigung bei Fehlern.
  • Plugins für Datenbanken (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite), Skripte und Excel-Dateien, neben den eingebauten Nodes der Node-Referenz.
  • Betrieb: Anmeldung mit Rollen, eine REST-API und das Kommandozeilenprogramm, ein Audit-Log und das Benutzerportal für Anwender, die nur Workflows ausführen.

docs.title: Update
docs.text: Erste Version, es gibt nichts zu aktualisieren.

docs.title: Administratorhandbuch
docs.text:
Dieses Handbuch richtet sich an Personen, die gView.Pipe installieren und betreiben.

  • Installation: ZIP und Docker, erster Start.
  • Konfiguration: Einstellungen, Ordner, Umgebungsvariablen.
  • Anmeldung: Anmeldung mit festen Benutzern oder einem Identity Provider (OIDC).
  • Plugins: welche Plugins es gibt und wie man sie installiert.
  • Skripte ausführen: Skriptordner und Git-Server freigeben.
  • Betrieb: Reverse Proxy, Webhooks, Backup, Updates, Logs.
  • Sicherheit: was die App schützt und was du schützen musst.
  • Fehlersuche: typische Probleme und ihre Ursachen.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: Skripte und CI-Pipelines nutzen die REST API unter /api/v1, um Workflows auszuführen, Executions abzufragen und Workflows zu deployen. Die API hat eigene Schlüssel; die Anmeldung der UI nutzt sie nie.

docs.title: API-Schlüssel
docs.text:
Schlüssel legst du auf der Seite API keys an (Navigation). Ein Schlüssel hat:

Einstellung Bedeutung Name Wer oder was ihn nutzt, z. B. CI Deploy. Mit dem Schlüssel gestartete Läufe zeigen in der Historie API · CI Deploy. Rights Read: Workflows, Executions, Gruppen. Run: Läufe starten, stoppen, wiederholen. Deploy: Workflows anlegen, ändern, löschen, aktivieren. Portal: nur die Portal-Endpunkte für das Anwender-Portal; allein verwenden. Only these groups Beschränkt den Schlüssel auf die Workflows dieser Gruppen. Andere Workflows sieht er gar nicht, auch keine ohne Gruppe. Expires Nach diesem Tag wird der Schlüssel abgelehnt. Leer: nie.

Der Schlüssel (pipe_…) wird einmal angezeigt, beim Anlegen. Gespeichert wird nur sein SHA-256 (data/api-keys.json); ein verlorener Schlüssel lässt sich also nicht mehr anzeigen: Lösche ihn und lege einen neuen an. Am Präfix pipe_ erkennen Secret-Scanner, z. B. von GitHub, versehentlich eingecheckte Schlüssel.

Schicke den Schlüssel als Header:

X-Pipe-Api-Key: pipe_…

oder als Authorization: Bearer pipe_….

Warning

Nur Benutzer mit der Rolle admin können Schlüssel anlegen. Mit Pipe:Auth:Mode none ist jeder admin, der die UI erreicht. Schütze die UI mit einer Anmeldung, bevor du dich auf Schlüssel verlässt. Mehr als 60 Fehlversuche pro Minute von einer Adresse werden mit 429 beantwortet.

docs.title: Endpunkte
docs.text:
Die API ist in /api/v1/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3) beschrieben. Lade die Datei in ein Werkzeug deiner Wahl, z. B. Postman, Bruno oder einen OpenAPI-Viewer, um die Endpunkte auszuprobieren.

Methode und Pfad Recht Macht GET /api/v1/workflows read Listet die Workflows. GET /api/v1/workflows/{id} read Der Workflow als JSON, mit seiner Version als ETag. PUT /api/v1/workflows/{id} deploy Legt den Workflow an oder ersetzt ihn (siehe unten). DELETE /api/v1/workflows/{id} deploy Löscht den Workflow. GET /api/v1/workflows/{id}/versions read Die gespeicherten Versionen, neueste zuerst, mit einer Zusammenfassung jeder Änderung. POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/activate, /deactivate deploy Schaltet seine Trigger ein oder aus. POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/run run Startet einen Lauf (siehe unten). GET /api/v1/executions read Executions, die neueste zuerst. Filter: workflowId, status, mode, from, before, limit. GET /api/v1/executions/{workflowId}/{id} read Eine Execution mit Eingabe, Ausgabe und Logs jedes Nodes. POST /api/v1/executions/{workflowId}/{id}/cancel run Stoppt einen laufenden oder wartenden Lauf. POST /api/v1/executions/{workflowId}/{id}/replay run Führt die Execution erneut aus; Body { "fromNodeId": "…" }, um an einem Node zu beginnen (Replay). GET /api/v1/groups read Listet die Workflow-Gruppen. GET /api/v1/audit read Das Audit-Log, die neuesten zuerst. Filter: from, before, actor, area, objectId, limit. Nur für Schlüssel ohne Gruppen-Beschränkung.

Fehler werden als application/problem+json beantwortet, mit einem title, der sagt, was nicht stimmt.

docs.title: Einen Workflow ausführen
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/run
{ "items": [ { "name": "Ada" } ], "environment": "TEST", "wait": true, "timeoutSeconds": 30 }

Alle Felder sind optional. Der Lauf startet an allen Nodes ohne eingehende Verbindung, mit items als deren Eingabe (Vorgabe: ein leeres Item). Er verhält sich wie ein getriggerter Lauf: Angeheftete Daten werden ignoriert, der Fehler-Workflow startet bei einem Fehler, und die Warteschlange des Workflows gilt (Max queued runs).

Antwort Wann 200 { executionId, status, error, errorNode, node, items } wait und der Lauf endete rechtzeitig; items ist die Ausgabe des zuletzt beendeten Nodes. Auch ein fehlgeschlagener Lauf ist 200, mit status: "error". 202 { executionId, status } Ohne wait, oder der Lauf dauert länger als timeoutSeconds; frag später GET /executions/{workflowId}/{executionId}. 429 Der Workflow läuft schon, und seine Warteschlange ist voll.

docs.title: Einen Workflow deployen
docs.text:
PUT /api/v1/workflows/{id} nimmt das JSON eines Workflows, wie GET es liefert oder wie es in data/workflows liegt. Vor dem Speichern wird geprüft: eindeutige Node-Ids und -Namen, Verbindungen zwischen vorhandenen Nodes, keine Zyklen, installierte Node-Typen, gültige Parameter. Probleme werden mit 422 und einer Liste in details.errors beantwortet. Credentials, die es auf diesem Server nicht gibt, stehen als details.warnings in der Antwort, sind aber keine Fehler.

Schicke If-Match mit dem ETag eines GET, um sicherzugehen, dass niemand den Workflow zwischendurch geändert hat; sonst bekommst du 412. Ohne If-Match wird der Workflow ersetzt. Ist der Workflow aktiv, werden seine Trigger mit der neuen Version neu geladen.

docs.title: Beispiele
docs.text:
curlPowerShell 
KEY=pipe_...
# ausführen und auf das Ergebnis warten
curl -s -X POST https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/workflows/hello-pipe/run \
  -H "X-Pipe-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "items": [ { "name": "Ada" } ], "wait": true }'

# einen Workflow aus einer Datei deployen
curl -s -X PUT https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/workflows/hello-pipe \
  -H "X-Pipe-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @hello-pipe.json

# die letzten fehlgeschlagenen Läufe
curl -s "https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/executions?status=error&limit=10" -H "X-Pipe-Api-Key: $KEY"

$headers = @{ "X-Pipe-Api-Key" = "pipe_..." }
# ausführen und auf das Ergebnis warten
$body = @{ items = @(@{ name = "Ada" }); wait = $true } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/workflows/hello-pipe/run `
  -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body

# einen Workflow aus einer Datei deployen
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put -Uri https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/workflows/hello-pipe `
  -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -InFile hello-pipe.json

# die letzten fehlgeschlagenen Läufe
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://pipe.example.com/api/v1/executions?status=error&limit=10" -Headers $headers
